faq.purposeA: Metrixify looks at your diary metrics day by day and asks: “When metric A goes up or down, does metric B often do the same?” The goal is hints for your life — not a medical diagnosis. A bright link on the map means: “worth paying attention to this pair.”
faq.howSearchA: Step 1: everything is grouped by calendar day (one value per metric per day). Step 2: we take every pair of metrics (sleep ↔ mood, nuts ↔ rash, and so on). Step 3: for each pair we only use days where both metrics were recorded. Step 4: we check whether they move together, opposite, or randomly. Step 5: the result is one number and one color on the map. You need at least 7 shared days for a preview; 14+ days is more reliable.
faq.howSearchExample: Example: Mon — nuts yes, rash 4 · Tue — nuts no, rash 1 · Wed — nuts yes, rash 3. Pattern: with nuts, rash is often higher → the link gets a positive score.
faq.pairsQ: Do we only check pairs of two metrics?
faq.pairsA: Yes, for now. We ask separately: nuts ↔ rash, sleep ↔ mood, TikTok ↔ energy, etc. If your bad day is caused by five things at once, each alone may look weak and the “combo” may not show up. Pairs are a simple first filter — “what to look at next” — not the full picture of your life.
faq.heatmapQ: How is the pattern map built?
faq.heatmapA: Each row and column is a metric name. A cell is the link strength between those two metrics (for the filters you picked above). The diagonal (same metric × same metric) is empty — it is not a real link. We only fill the upper triangle; the mirror half is the same number. Color = how strong the link is (pale → bright blue). Direction (together or opposite) appears when you hover.
faq.readMapQ: How do I read the map?
faq.readMapA: Find the row of one metric and the column of another — or just hover a square. Brighter blue = stronger pattern. Tooltip shows names and whether they move together (+) or opposite (−). “Weaker → Stronger” at the bottom is about strength, not good vs bad. Many metrics on one map gets crowded — the map works best with a small set.
faq.numbersA: A simple thermometer from −1 to +1. Plus = they often move the same way (both up or both down). Minus = often opposite (one up, other down). Near zero = no clear pattern. +0.60 means “often together, but not always.” −1 or +1 almost never happens in real diaries. This is not “60% your fault” — only how steady the pattern is.
faq.numbersExample: Example: +0.60 — on most days with nuts, rash is higher; some days break the rule. −0.40 — when screen time rises, sleep quality often drops, but not every day.
faq.filtersQ: What do the two dropdowns mean?
faq.filtersA: “What to compare”: Proportional change — good when both are numbers on a scale (sleep hours and mood 1–5). Same direction — good for yes/no and “both rise or fall together” even if not by the same amount. “When to compare”: Same day — both on one date. Next-day link — first metric today, second tomorrow. Previous-day link — the reverse.
faq.limitsQ: What can Metrixify not find yet?
faq.limitsA: Not a chain of causes (“A caused B caused C”). Not “five small factors added up” — only pairs. Not slow buildup like sleep debt over two weeks unless it shows in daily numbers. Not proof that one thing caused another — only that they appear together in your diary. Correlation ≠ causation.

correlations.causationDisclaimer: Correlation does not imply causation. Patterns may reflect coincidence, shared causes, or diary bias.
correlations.dailyAggDisclaimer: Analysis uses daily aggregates (ordinal mean, numeric sum, boolean any-true). Intraday detail is rolled up per day.
correlations.minSampleNote: Exploratory pairs need at least 7 shared daily points; 14+ days are recommended for more stable correlations.
